key_insight: A self-supervised functional autoencoder learns a reusable latent space, separating function representation from task-specific neural operator training.
engineering_relevance: For solid-mechanics surrogates, frozen representations can reduce training memory and accelerate inference without rebuilding the function representation for each task.
method: Pre-train on analytically generated functions without solvers or labels.
Encode arbitrary point clouds with exact translation, dilation, and amplitude equivariance.
Freeze the encoder and decoder, then train task-specific operators on cached embeddings.
evidence_signal: Across 28 tasks spanning solid mechanics, fluids, acoustics, Helmholtz, and Poisson equations, the abstract reports accuracy that can exceed state-of-the-art end-to-end models and up to an order-of-magnitude higher throughput.
watch_item: Transfer to a specific mechanics application still requires validation of reconstruction fidelity and operator accuracy on its geometries and loading regimes.
paper_title: Self-Supervised Learning of Universal Latent Spaces for Operator Learning
